contests.title: Kansas City — Parks and infrastructure sales tax

provenance.quote: Shall the City of Kansas City, Kansas, be authorized to impose an additional three-eighths of one percent citywide retailers' sales tax the proceeds of which shall be used as follows: 1) approximately fifty percent (50%) for the purposes of financing park capital improvement projects, including parks, community centers and trails, and 2) approximately fifty percent (50%) for the purposes of financing infrastructure projects such as roads, bridges, and sidewalks, the collection of such Sales Tax commencing on April 1, 2027, or as soon thereafter as permitted by law, and terminating ten years after its commencement?

provenance.sourceOrg: Douglas County Clerk and Election Officer
provenance.quote: Shall the City of Lawrence, Kansas be authorized to repeal the 2019 Sales Tax in the amount of two tenths of one percent (0.2%) in the City of Lawrence, Kansas, and replace it with the levying of a new special purpose retailers’ sales tax in the amount of three tenths of one percent (0.3%) for the purposes of operating a City Public Transit System, including purchasing and maintaining buses and other transit vehicles, constructing and maintaining transit facilities, and purchasing and maintaining equipment and such other related Public Transit purposes as may be in the best interest of the City, with such special purpose retailers’ sale tax to take effect on the 1st day of April, 2027, if approved by a majority of the qualified electors voting thereon. The new special purpose retailers’ sales tax referenced herein, if approved by a majority of the qualified electors voting thereon, shall expire after ten (10) years from the date upon which such tax is first collected. [Note: In the event that the new special purpose retailers’ sales tax referenced herein is not approved by a majority of the qualified electors voting thereon at the November 3, 2026, general election, then the 2019 Sales Tax shall not be repealed and shall remain in full force and effect until it expires in accordance with the terms of Ordinance No. 9549.]

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a new countywide 0.25% sales tax to help pay for health care, including care for people who cannot afford it, mental-health and substance-use services, preventive care and the county health department. Collection would start April 1, 2027, or as soon afterward as the law allows. The question sets no end date.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the countywide 0.25% sales tax for health-care services.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this health-care sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a 0.375% sales tax within Kansas City for ten years. About half the money would go to parks, community centers and trails, and about half to infrastructure such as roads, bridges and sidewalks. Collection would begin April 1, 2027, or as soon afterward as the law allows, and end ten years after it starts.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional 0.375% city sales tax for these purposes and ten-year term.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional city sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces Lawrence’s existing 0.2% transit sales tax with a 0.3% tax, an increase of 0.1 percentage point. The new tax would pay to run the city transit system and buy or maintain vehicles, facilities and equipment. It would start April 1, 2027, and end ten years after collection begins. If the proposal fails, the existing 0.2% tax would continue until its scheduled expiration under the current ordinance.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Replace the existing 0.2% transit sales tax with the new 0.3% tax for ten years.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the existing 0.2% transit sales tax until it expires under the current ordinance.
